successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy entity interface is exported from the policy module barrel and uses the canonical camelCase field set with leaveType typed as the LeaveType enum imported from shared types.
findById returns a fully mapped LeavePolicy (snake_case row → camelCase entity) when a row exists, and returns null when no row matches.
findByLeaveType returns an array of mapped LeavePolicy entities for the given leave type; it returns an empty array (never null) when no policies match.
findAllActive returns only policies where is_active is true; it returns an empty array (never null) when no active policies exist.
create persists a new row via INSERT with NOW() for created_at and updated_at, and returns the created LeavePolicy entity mapped from the returned row.

update applies only supplied mutable fields via a dynamic SET clause (excluding id, createdAt, updatedAt from the mutable allowlist), falls back to a read of the existing row when no mutable fields are supplied, and returns null when no row matches the id.
deactivate sets is_active to false and updated_at to NOW(), returning true when a row was affected (rowCount > 0) and false when no row matched.
Every repository query uses parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, …) for all user-supplied or entity-supplied values; no value is interpolated into the SQL string.
Database errors (connection failures, constraint violations, permission errors) propagate as rejected promises from every repository method; no error is swallowed or silently caught.

The Jest test suite at tests/unit/modules/policy/policy.repository.test.ts covers each repository method with happy-path (asserting mapped entity + exact SQL + params), not-found/null, empty-array, and error-propagation cases, and all tests pass.
The module compiles under strict TypeScript (strict: true) with zero `any` types — query parameter arrays are typed as unknown[] and row casts use type-safe narrowing.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001); the policy repository is the only component that issues SQL against the leave_policies table.
No `any` type anywhere in the policy module (HARNESS no-any, severity high) — use `unknown` with type guards and type parameter arrays as `unknown[]`.
All SQL queries must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, …) for every value; no string interpolation or concatenation of values into SQL (SQL-injection prevention).
Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) must be set by the database via NOW() in INSERT and UPDATE statements, never supplied as application-side Date values.
The policy module may only depend on src/shared/types and src/shared/db — it is a foundation module with zero domain-module dependencies (acyclic dependency rule).
Modules must import from each other only through their declared public entry point (index.ts barrel); no cross-module imports of internal files.

Tests must use bare-path imports (modules/policy/policy.repository, shared/db/connection, shared/types/index) with no src/ prefix and no relative paths, matching jest.config.js moduleDirectories: ['node_modules', 'src'].
Test files must follow the project Jest convention: *.test.ts under tests/, matching testMatch ['**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)'] — not .spec.ts.
The LeavePolicy entity must be a standalone camelCase interface that does NOT extend BaseEntity (BaseEntity uses snake_case created_at/updated_at; domain entities use camelCase createdAt/updatedAt).
outOfScope: Policy service layer (IPolicyService / PolicyService) — deferred to a later phase; this phase builds only model + repository + barrel.
Policy controller and routes (HTTP translation, Fastify plugin registration) — deferred to later phases.
Zod validation schemas for policy inputs (policy.validation.ts) — deferred to the validation-schemas phase.
Audit record creation (GP-002) for policy create/update/deactivate — the repository layer does not write audit records; audit is a service-layer concern deferred to later phases.
RBAC enforcement (GP-005) on policy operations — no HTTP endpoints exist in this phase; RBAC is enforced at the route/middleware layer in later phases.
Database migrations / DDL (CREATE TABLE leave_policies) — migrations are generated separately by the code agent; this phase assumes the leave_policies table schema exists.
Integration tests against a real PostgreSQL instance — this phase includes only Jest unit tests with a mocked pool.query.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeavePolicy's lifecycle is ACTIVE → INACTIVE; deactivation is the only state transition and is irreversible through the repository (there is no reactivate method). The isActive flag is the sole lifecycle indicator.
The leaveType field must be one of the six LeaveType enum members (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity); the repository casts the stored string back to the LeaveType enum on read.

The id, createdAt, and updatedAt fields are immutable through update — the mutable-field allowlist excludes them; only business fields (policyName, leaveType, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive) may be changed.

The nullable numeric fields (accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays) may be null or a non-negative number; the repository must preserve null values through create and update without coercion.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns LeavePolicy | null; null when no row matches. Database errors propagate as rejected promises (not swallowed).
Returns LeavePolicy[] (empty array, never null, when no match). Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Returns LeavePolicy[] (empty array, never null, when no active policies). Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Returns the created LeavePolicy. Unique-constraint / check-constraint violations propagate as rejected promises.

Returns LeavePolicy | null. When no mutable fields are supplied, falls back to a read (findById) and returns the existing entity or null. Returns null when no row matches the id. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.
Returns boolean: true when a row was affected (rowCount > 0), false when no row matched. Database errors propagate as rejected promises.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The policy repository must mirror the employee repository's structural pattern: an interface + implementation class, an internal snake_case Row interface, a mapRowToEntity helper, a camelToSnake helper, parameterized pool.query calls, a dynamic-SET update with a mutableFields allowlist and empty-partial fallback to findById, and a boolean-returning terminal operation (deactivate ≡ employee softDelete) driven by rowCount.

The LeavePolicy.leaveType field must be typed as the LeaveType enum imported from shared types (not a raw string), and the repository must cast the stored leave_type string back to LeaveType on read — matching how the employee repository casts employment_status to EmploymentStatus.

The policy repository must obtain its database connection by importing the existing `pool` export from shared/db/connection — it must not instantiate its own Pool or use a different connection mechanism.

The policy barrel (index.ts) must re-export the entity interface, the repository interface, and the repository class — matching the employee barrel's export surface (entity + interface + implementation).

The policy test file must follow the employee test's conventions: jest.mock('shared/db/connection') with a mocked pool.query, makeRow() (snake_case) and makePolicy() (camelCase) helpers, per-method describe blocks, and coverage of happy-path (exact SQL + params via toHaveBeenCalledWith), not-found/null, empty-array, and error-propagation cases.

The LeavePolicy entity field set and the leave_policies table column set must match the reconciled architecture exactly: id, policy_name/policyName, leave_type/leaveType, entitlement_days/entitlementDays, accrual_rate/accrualRate, max_accumulation/maxAccumulation, minimum_notice_days/minimumNoticeDays, requires_manager_approval/requiresManagerApproval, is_active/isActive, created_at/createdAt, updated_at/updatedAt — no foreign keys.

integrationPoints.why: The policy module imports the LeaveType enum to type the leaveType field and to cast the stored string back on read.
The policy repository imports the shared `pool` (pg Pool) to execute all SQL against the leave_policies table.
The policy module mirrors the employee module's repository pattern (interface + class, Row mapping, camelToSnake, dynamic SET, boolean terminal op) to maintain cross-module consistency.

The balance module will depend on the policy module (via its barrel) to look up LeavePolicy entitlement and accrual configuration; the policy barrel's public export surface is the contract balance will consume.
The leave orchestrator will depend on the policy module to resolve LeavePolicy by leaveTypeId for minimumNoticeDays enforcement and requiresManagerApproval auto-approval logic.
